subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the Eduqas spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE Eduqas Biology simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Cell division and the cell cycle

questions.q: Which feature is found in a prokaryotic cell such as a bacterium but NOT in a eukaryotic cell?
options: A single circular loop of DNA free in the cytoplasm
questions.explain: Prokaryotic cells have no true nucleus; their DNA is a single circular chromosome free in the cytoplasm, often with small plasmids. Eukaryotic cells keep DNA in a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.q: Which set of structures is found in a plant cell but NOT in a typical animal cell?
questions.explain: Plant cells additionally have a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts (for photosynthesis) and a large permanent vacuole containing cell sap. Animal cells lack all three.

questions.q: What is the function of the mitochondria?
options: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
Site of aerobic respiration to release energy
questions.explain: Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, releasing energy from glucose. Ribosomes make proteins; the cell membrane controls entry/exit; the nucleus stores DNA.

questions.q: Where in a cell does protein synthesis take place?
questions.explain: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis. They may be free in the cytoplasm or attached to membranes.

questions.q: A cell has a real diameter of 0.05 mm. Under a microscope its image is 10 mm wide. What is the magnification?
questions.explain: Magnification = image size / real size = 10 mm / 0.05 mm = x200. Always convert to the same units first.

questions.q: An image of a cell is 40 mm long at a magnification of x400. What is the real length of the cell?
questions.explain: Real size = image size / magnification = 40 mm / 400 = 0.1 mm, which is 100 micrometres.

questions.q: Why can an electron microscope reveal more detail than a light microscope?
options: It has a much higher magnification and resolution
It uses visible light more efficiently
questions.explain: Electron microscopes have far higher magnification AND resolution (resolving power), so they can distinguish sub-cellular structures that a light microscope cannot separate.

questions.lo: Cell division and the cell cycle
questions.q: During which stage of the cell cycle are the chromosomes copied (DNA replicated)?
questions.explain: DNA is replicated during interphase, before mitosis begins, so that each new cell receives a full copy of the genetic material.

questions.lo: Cell division and the cell cycle
questions.q: Mitosis produces two new cells that are:
options: Genetically different, with half the chromosomes
Genetically identical to the parent cell, with the full number of chromosomes
questions.explain: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells, each with the full (diploid) chromosome number. It is used for growth, repair and asexual reproduction.

questions.q: What is a stem cell?
options: An undifferentiated cell that can divide and differentiate into other cell types
A fully specialised cell that cannot divide
A cell found only in bacteria
questions.explain: A stem cell is an undifferentiated cell capable of dividing and differentiating into specialised cell types. Embryonic stem cells can form any type; adult stem cells are more limited.

questions.q: Which is a potential MEDICAL benefit of using stem cells?
options: Replacing damaged or diseased cells, e.g. in treating diabetes or paralysis
questions.explain: Stem cells can differentiate into needed cell types, so they may replace damaged/diseased cells (e.g. producing insulin-secreting cells for diabetes, or nerve cells for spinal injuries).

questions.q: Which word equation correctly represents aerobic respiration?
options: glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water (+ energy)
questions.explain: Aerobic respiration: glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water, releasing energy. It occurs in the mitochondria and requires oxygen.

questions.q: Aerobic respiration is an example of which type of reaction?
questions.explain: Respiration is exothermic - it releases energy (transferred from glucose) for the cell to use in processes such as movement, growth and keeping warm.

questions.q: What are the products of anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
questions.explain: In human muscle, anaerobic respiration converts glucose to lactic acid, releasing a small amount of energy without oxygen. It happens during vigorous exercise.

questions.q: Anaerobic respiration in yeast (fermentation) produces:
questions.explain: In yeast, anaerobic respiration (fermentation) produces ethanol and carbon dioxide. This is used in brewing and bread-making.

questions.q: Enzymes are biological catalysts. This means they:
options: Are used up during the reaction
Only work at very high temperatures
Speed up reactions without being used up
questions.explain: Enzymes are proteins that act as biological catalysts, speeding up reactions without being used up. Their specific shape lets substrates fit the active site (lock and key).

questions.q: A student measures enzyme activity as temperature rises. Above the optimum, activity falls sharply because the enzyme:
options: Uses up all the substrate instantly
Is denatured - its active site changes shape
questions.explain: Above the optimum temperature the enzyme denatures: bonds break and the active site changes shape, so the substrate no longer fits and the reaction rate falls.

questions.q: How does a change in pH away from the optimum usually affect an enzyme?
options: It can denature the enzyme, changing the active site shape
It converts the enzyme to a lipid
questions.explain: A pH far from the enzyme's optimum can denature it, altering the active site so the substrate no longer binds, lowering activity.

questions.q: DNA is described as a double helix. What is a gene?
options: A short section of DNA that codes for a protein
questions.explain: A gene is a section of DNA that codes for a particular sequence of amino acids, and therefore a specific protein. DNA is arranged as a double helix within chromosomes.

questions.q: In a food test, which reagent turns from blue to brick-red on heating to show a reducing sugar such as glucose?
questions.explain: Benedict's solution turns from blue to brick-red (via green/orange) when heated with a reducing sugar. Iodine tests for starch (blue-black); Biuret tests for protein (purple).
